problem: Embodied navigation methods (end-to-end, modular, or LLM-based) are tied to task-specific architectures and need retraining or manual module changes for each new task. Prior LLM navigators lack a compositional structure, while VisProg/ViperGPT-style program composition had only been applied to static images.
motivation: A single training-free system that composes primitives could handle many embodied tasks (open-vocabulary ObjNav, lifelong multi-goal navigation, EQA) and avoid the heavy training cost. Extending VisProg-style neuro-symbolic programs to interactive 3D navigation needs a robust navigation primitive plus memory for sequential goals.
key_idea: Use GPT-4o with 15 in-context examples to compose pre-trained primitives (detect, answer, match, navigate_to, explore_scene, etc.) into executable pseudo-programs, built around a PointNav policy and a VLFM-style exploration policy extended with a per-pixel feature memory.
insight: A generic set of primitives around PointNav and value-map exploration, sequenced by an LLM, transfers across tasks with no training, and the LLM's decomposition of descriptions into ordered sub-goals helps multi-modal lifelong navigation (attributed by the authors to the LLM rather than noisy text embeddings). The memory ablation on MultiON shows that a threshold of 0.4 gives +5 SR and +2 SPL over no memory. The failure analysis shows most errors come from detection (ignored or wrong object), not LLM planning (about 11% of EQA errors).
method: Program generation: GPT-4o receives 15 fixed in-context examples spanning ObjNav, GOAT and EQA, and outputs a commented step-by-step pseudo-program for the instruction, following the VisProg style rather than free-form code.

Primitive modules: each primitive parses its line and executes in the environment, updating program state. Python subroutines (count, is_found, eval) sit alongside vision models: OWLv2 or DETR for detect, a CLIP classifier to reduce false positives, SuperGlue for match on image goals, and BLIP2 for answer.
Navigation module: a pre-trained PointGoal policy (from HM3D, using depth and a relative goal vector) drives waypoint navigation; detected-object box centers plus depth give the waypoint.

Exploration with memory (explore_scene): VLFM frontier exploration with a BLIP2 language-grounded value map, extended with a per-pixel feature map. When the target changes, the value map is recomputed by cosine similarity with the new text or image embedding, and the agent goes straight to a remembered location if the max value exceeds a threshold (0.4).
Agent and action interface: Habitat with actions Forward, Move Left/Right, Look Up/Down and Stop. Explainability comes from LLM comments and per-module outputs, used for manual failure analysis.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) planner + frozen OWLv2/DETR, CLIP, BLIP2, SuperGlue + pre-trained PointNav policy and VLFM exploration
setting.training_data: none (training-free); only the PointNav policy is pre-trained on HM3D train scenes, which are not used for evaluation
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: Forward 0.25 m, turns 30°, look up/down, stop; PointNav waypoints

numbers.extra: similar answers grouped (answer constraint); supplementary preliminary experiment. Without constraint QA Top-1 is 42/40/38/37
numbers.evidence: Supplementary Table MP3D-EQA results, row TANGO +answer constraint

numbers_note: Split for OpenEQA is not explicitly named in the paper; 'test' is used as a placeholder. MP3D-EQA split is likewise unstated; 'val' is used as a placeholder. The MultiON memory ablation is reported in the supplement (not listed in numbers).
results: TANGO gets SR 35.5 / SPL 19.5 on HM3D-OVON val-unseen, on par with VLFM (35.2/19.6) and just below DAgRL+OD (37.1/19.9). On GOAT-Bench it reaches SR 32.1, beating SenseAct-NN Skill Chain (29.5), with SPL 16.5 second to Modular GOAT (17.2). On OpenEQA it scores 37.2, second to Socratic LLMs w/ Frame Captions (38.1) and far below humans (85.1).
limitations: Depends on GPT-4o, with LLM planning errors on complex or ambiguous prompts (about 18% of EQA failures) and detector failures such as ignoring or stopping at the wrong object as the main error source
The memory mechanism uses a simple max-value threshold (tuned on MultiON), and wrong memorized targets hurt efficiency; there is no ablation on the main benchmarks beyond MultiON
Does not cover VLN, and results are near or below the best specialized or trained baselines rather than clearly better; only closed-source GPT-4o is tested
compares_to: GOAT-Bench baselines (SenseAct-NN, Modular GOAT, Modular CLIP on Wheels)
